key_type.description: key type registered on substrate (ed25519 or sr25519)

network.description: grid network, one of: dev test qa main

rmb_timeout.description: timeout duration in seconds for rmb calls

ip_range.description: IP range of the node for the wireguard network (e.g. 10.1.2.0/24). Has to have a subnet mask of 24.

name.description: Solution name for created contract to be consistent across threefold tooling. Must contain only alphanumeric and underscore characters.

network_name.description: Network name of the deployed network resource to connect vms.

node.description: Node id to place the deployment on.

solution_provider.description: Solution provider ID for the deployed solution which allows the creator of the solution to gain a percentage of the rewards.

solution_type.description: Solution type for created contract to be consistent across threefold tooling.

name.description: Disk workload name. This has to be unique within the deployment. Must contain only alphanumeric and underscore characters.

size.description: Disk size in GBs. Must be between 1GB and 10240GBs (10TBs)

cache.description: The size of the fuse mountpoint on the node in MBs (holds qsfs local data before pushing).

compression_algorithm.description: configuration to use for the compression stage. Currently only snappy is supported.

encryption_algorithm.description: configuration to use for the encryption stage. Currently only AES is supported.

expected_shards.description: The amount of shards which are generated when the data is encoded. Essentially, this is the amount of shards which is needed to be able to recover the data, and some disposable shards which could be lost. The amount of disposable shards can be calculated as expected_shards - minimal_shards.

max_zdb_data_dir_size.description: Maximum size of the data dir in MiB, if this is set and the sum of the file sizes in the data dir gets higher than this value, the least used, already encoded file will be removed.

minimal_shards.description: The minimum amount of shards which are needed to recover the original data.

name.description: Qsfs workload name. This has to be unique within the deployment. Must contain only alphanumeric and underscore characters.

redundant_groups.description: The amount of groups which one should be able to loose while still being able to recover the original data.

redundant_nodes.description: The amount of nodes that can be lost in every group while still being able to recover the original data.

block.description: The backend groups to write the data to.

encryption_algorithm.description: configuration to use for the encryption stage. Currently only AES is supported.

prefix.description: Data stored on the remote metadata is prefixed with.

type.description: configuration for the metadata store to use, currently only ZDB is supported.

block.description:

computedip.description: The reserved public ipv4 if any.

computedip6.description: The reserved public ipv6 if any.

gpus.description: List of the GPUs to be attached to the vm and must not be used by other vms

memory.description: Memory size in MB. Must be between 256MBs and 262144MBs (256GBs).

rootfs_size.description: Root file system size in MB. Must be between 1024MBs and 10485760MBs (10TBs).

mount_point.description: Directory to mount the disk on inside the ZMachine.

block.description: List of vm (ZMachine) mounts. Can reference QSFSs and Disks.

ips.description: Computed IPs of the ZDB. Two IPs are returned: a public IPv6, and a YggIP, in this order

mode.description: Mode of the ZDB, `user` or `seq`. `user` is the default mode where a user can SET their own keys, like any key-value store. All keys are kept in memory. in `seq` mode, keys are sequential and autoincremented.

public.description: Makes it read-only if password is set, writable if no password set.

size.description: Size of the ZDB in GBs.

block.description: List of ZDB workloads configurations. You can read more about 0-db (ZDB) [here](https://github.com/threefoldtech/0-db/).

A user should have some fully qualified domain name (fqdn) (e.g. example.com), pointing to the specified node working as a gateway, then connect this gateway to whichever backend services they desire, making these backend services accessible through the computed fqdn.

block.description: Resource to deploy a network on the grid. This is a private wireguard network. A user could specify that they want to have a user access endpoint to this network through the `add_wg_access` flag. A separate workload is deployed on each of the specified nodes, with the peers for each workload configured in a way making any pair of nodes in the network accessible to each other.
